definitions.explanation: One of the Japanese syllabary writing systems, typically used for foreign words and emphasis.

examples.japanese: {片仮名|かたかな}を{覚|おぼ}える。
この{言葉|ことば}は{片仮名|かたかな}で{書|か}きます。
examples.english: This word is written in katakana.

examples.japanese: {外国|がいこく}の{名前|なまえ}は{片仮名|かたかな}で{書|か}きます。
examples.english: Foreign names are written in katakana.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のとき、{平仮名|ひらがな}より{片仮名|かたかな}のほうが{難|むずか}しかった。
examples.english: When I was a child, katakana was harder than hiragana.

notes:
One of the three Japanese writing systems. {片仮名|かたかな} characters are angular in shape, derived from parts of {漢字|かんじ}. Also written as カタカナ in casual use.

MAIN USES:
- Foreign loanwords (コーヒー, テレビ)
- Onomatopoeia (ガタガタ, ワンワン)
- Emphasis (similar to italics in English)
- Scientific and technical names
- Company and brand names

JAPANESE SCRIPTS:
- {平仮名|ひらがな}: hiragana (native Japanese words, grammar)
- {片仮名|かたかな}: katakana (loanwords, emphasis)
- {漢字|かんじ}: kanji (Chinese characters)

NOTE:
The word {片|かた} means "partial" or "one of a pair," distinguishing it from {平|ひら} (plain/ordinary) in {平仮名|ひらがな}.
